lines: Three lines chalked out and no deep fish on this stall since spring.
Every deep-water skipper I buy from is beached with a full year's charter
paid up front by somebody who does not want the boat used. Work that one out.
Nine tons a day, this city. Nine. I do about a hundredth of it.
You want to feel small, do not climb the tower. Stand behind this stall.
Wool from the west, linen from the wetlands, and the good stuff off a ship.
The girl measures against her arm because somebody walked off with the yard.
She is within a thumb every time and it drives the inspector to distraction.
They are not Aurelian and I will say so to anybody who asks.
Nobody asks. They just want a spiral to put on the mantelpiece.
Forty years I have sold spirals to people who never once asked what they meant.
Everybody in Aureline has a Kin and nobody in Aureline has any grass.
That is the whole of my trade and it will see me out.
Rings when a cart goes past. I stopped hearing it in about my second year.
My wife says I have stopped hearing several other things since.
The shelf that says it does not work outsells the rest of the stall.
I could take the label off and sell twice as much and I am not going to.
There is a clinic four streets away and it is free. Go there first.
Nine weeks from the Sunder Isles and that is not the far side of anything.
There are leagues out there with Kin nobody here has a name for.
Caelora is a coastline, friend. Averra is the rest of it.
Four hundred and twelve stalls and I use the same eleven every week.
You do that here. You make a village out of it or it eats you.
Weights, measures, and the honesty of a chalk board. That is my entire remit.
Aureline is scrupulous about a pound of flour and cheerfully vague
about almost everything else, and I have never worked out why.
Under the glass roof it comes back at you twice.
The market inspector says I need a licence. The baker says I do not.
I have decided to believe the baker.
Tuesdays and Fridays for thirty years and I could tell you every stallholder's
children's names.
None of them could tell you mine, and that is the fairest deal in the building.
